title: sharedstat: diagnose and correct statistics built from a shared component
description:
An R package accompanying a study of statistics formed from a difference, ratio or residual of two quantities that share a component. Four such constructions are covered: a divergence measured against a shared reference arm, a trans term obtained by subtracting a cis term, a count of significant features read as an ordering of effect sizes, and an interaction contrast on compositional counts.

The package provides the two estimators, the attenuation result, the five admission checks and a known-truth simulator in which compositionality emerges from closed-sum sampling rather than being imposed as an offset. Its central analytical result is that when one noisy reference is used both as the regression predictor and as a component of the contrast, the naive estimator returns the true gain multiplied by the reference arm's reliability, so an apparent divergence is produced even when the true divergence is exactly zero, and the direction of a conclusion inverts once the reliability falls below the reciprocal of the gain.

The test suite asserts the values printed in the accompanying paper rather than internal invariants, so a failing test means the package and the paper have diverged. Six further tests pin behaviour that was wrong during development and is now fixed, because a test that only asserts current behaviour cannot catch a regression to a defect that has already occurred once.

It ranks no method as more accurate than another and describes no standard method as biased. What it provides is the size of each artefact relative to the effect being estimated, and the procedure that follows from it.

This record archives the version the paper's results were computed with. Later development continues in the linked repository.
